cohort: Human cervicovaginal epithelial cells (HeLa cells, ATCC 35241) cultured in monolayers.
finding: Infection of cervicovaginal epithelial cells by U. urealyticum stimulates ammonia production and elevated IL-8, leading to significantly higher cytotoxicity, while L. crispatus appeared protective against inflammation and death, producing more D-lactate and less IL-8.
